synopsis:
A boy carrying a musical-theatre dream arrives at a place where performers come to pursue their ambitions, only to find that his empty wallet can afford him one room: #0528. The room bears the shadow of an earlier fire, and rumours claim that unsettling incidents have never ceased there. Once he moves in, uncanny events begin to crowd his everyday life, drawing him into an unforeseen fantasy. What first seems like a frightening haunting gradually becomes an encounter with the two ghosts tied to the room and its painful past. Living amid their pranks, secrets, and lingering emotions, the boy learns that the spirits are not simply figures of terror but companions burdened by unfinished attachments. As their lives intersect, the room becomes a refuge where fear yields to recognition, laughter, and mutual comfort. The boy’s determination to remain close to music and pursue a future onstage gains new meaning through the companionship he finds in #0528. The supernatural journey ultimately leads him toward emotional courage and a renewed willingness to meet the future.

The musical centres on dreams, companionship, and the healing possible when the living listen to those who have been left behind. Its one-human, two-ghost relationship turns an ostensibly eerie room into a space of warmth, hope, and new beginnings.

show: 音乐剧《Borderline-边界线》中文版(韩国 WELCOMEFUNNY 原版制作,原版总制作人 YOU HWAN WOONG,编剧 YUMIN,作曲 PARK JIYOUNG;中方出品/制作 缪时客,执行制作厂牌 M²,导演 Tobias Weis,剧本翻译 胡楚浩/Dylan Goike,韩语校对 静国玲;2026 年在上海长江剧场·红匣子演出。🚨 不是 Benjamin Velez 作曲、Aryanna Garber 编剧的那部美国原创音乐喜剧《BORDERLINE》,也不是任何以边缘型人格障碍(BPD)为题材的作品——那是同名的另一部戏,请勿混淆)。⚠ 请只描述【上面这一部制作】的剧情;如果找不到这部戏的资料,请直接说明找不到,【不要用同名或题材相近的其他作品】(小说、电影、电视剧、其他音乐剧或戏曲)的剧情来代替,也不要凭剧名推测
synopsis:
July arrives at Borderline’s headquarters determined to become the kind of agent who once saved him as a child. Twenty years after a devastating war has left civilisation in ruins, the organisation operates in a decayed city where formal justice has failed: it accepts contracts to execute those deemed beyond redemption and calls this work a necessary correction to a corrupt world. Newly promoted and assigned to a different office, July expects purpose, discipline, and heroic certainty. Instead, his new partner is June, a withdrawn, uncooperative killer whose poor record and apparent indifference make him everything July cannot understand.

Their superior, February—June’s longtime friend—explains that June was once feared throughout the city, a figure capable of making its most vicious criminals tremble. As July and June are forced to work together, their hostile partnership slowly becomes an irreplaceable bond. Yet the closer July comes to June and the deeper he enters Borderline’s operations, the more the organisation’s righteous self-image begins to fracture. Buried truths emerge, and July and June confront the cruelty concealed behind February’s benevolent façade, forcing them to decide where justice ends and murder begins.

The musical examines justice in a broken society, and the danger of claiming the authority to decide who deserves to die. It also pits idealism and loyalty against manipulation, violence, and the painful discovery that moral certainty may be a mask.

synopsis:
Lieutenant Piler arrives in Amsterdam at the end of the Second World War to take charge of a gallery that has been sealed by the authorities. What initially appears to be a routine postwar investigation soon exposes a transaction of startling consequence: the art dealer Van Meegeren has sold a painting regarded as a Dutch national treasure to Hermann Göring for an enormous sum. As the case unfolds, Professor Martin examines the evidence and concludes that Van Meegeren’s sale constitutes proof of treason. The accusation places the dealer at the centre of a public scandal, while the machinery of justice closes around him and the threat of execution becomes increasingly real. Van Meegeren must face not only the legal charge against him but also the judgement of a society emerging from occupation, where cultural loss, wartime complicity, and national humiliation remain painfully raw. His trial draws worldwide attention, turning one man’s disputed act in the art market into a larger reckoning with what was surrendered, bought, preserved, or betrayed during the war.

The musical centres on art as both a national symbol and a perilous form of currency. It examines guilt, truth, public judgement, and the uneasy boundary between survival, profiteering, and betrayal in the aftermath of war.

synopsis:
Wuyao pedals a bicycle through 1930s Beiping, barely earning enough to survive by carrying passengers as foreign aggression and political turmoil close in. By chance, he meets Dehou and Zijing, two young men whose temperaments and convictions differ sharply from his own. Drawn together by the urgency of their age, the three form an uneasy companionship and resolve to go to Shanghai, hoping that even their limited strength can contribute to resistance.

The journey tests the resolve behind that decision. Their shared indignation gives them moments of exhilarating solidarity, but their contrasting ways of seeing the world also generate conflict. As the three travel on, their arguments over ideals, reality, and what action can truly achieve expose fears and private burdens that each has carried alone. Yet hardship repeatedly forces them to rely on one another, transforming chance acquaintances into comrades whose friendship is tempered by sacrifice. Their individual choices, alternately impulsive and painful, reveal how ordinary people must decide whether to protect themselves or stand for something larger amid an era of upheaval.

The musical considers how youthful idealism survives when confronted with harsh reality. It also celebrates fellowship, moral courage, and the modest but meaningful power of people who refuse to surrender their convictions.

synopsis:
Chen Qizheng returns secretly to Jimei in 1938, carrying anti-Japanese war funds raised by the Nanyang Chinese community. The journey home immediately turns perilous when his luggage disappears, severing his control over the precious gold and placing him amid an invisible web of surveillance. In the wartime city, familiar faces offer neither simple safety nor certainty: old friendships become suspect, loyalties shift under pressure, and enemy agents close in. A trunk of gold becomes the central clue in a tightening mystery, drawing Chen Qizheng into conflicts between personal interest and conviction, private affection and the demands of the nation. Each encounter forces him to test whom he can trust and how much he is willing to sacrifice. As betrayals, concealed motives, and reversals surface, Chen Qizheng must decide whether to protect himself or risk his life to ensure that the funds reach those resisting the invasion. His choice reveals the human cost behind the overseas Chinese community’s support for the war and turns a dangerous homecoming into a reckoning with faith, responsibility, and survival.

The musical examines trust under occupation, the collision of individual desire with collective duty, and the endurance of patriotic commitment across distance. It frames Chen Qizheng’s ordeal as both a suspenseful search for the truth and a tribute to those whose sacrifices helped sustain resistance.

synopsis:
Vita meets Anubis on a journey through the realm of the dead, where a boy’s passage beyond life becomes intertwined with the duty of a guardian hound. As the two travel together, Anubis must protect Vita from the dangers and trials that lie along the way, while Vita confronts the fear, confusion, and longing that accompany separation from the world he has known. Their relationship develops through encounters that test trust and compassion: Anubis is not simply a terrifying god of death, but a watchful companion burdened with the responsibility of guiding souls; Vita is not merely a helpless traveller, but a young person whose feelings and choices give the journey its emotional force. Amid moments of darkness, the pair find humour, tenderness, and courage. Vita’s bond with Anubis gradually turns the passage through death into an experience of mutual care, as protection is offered, received, questioned, and ultimately understood. By facing what cannot be avoided, the boy learns to move forward, and the guardian discovers the human weight of the role he performs.

The musical centres on death as a journey rather than a simple ending, using the relationship between Vita and Anubis to consider fear, loss, and acceptance. It also emphasises guardianship and companionship: even in an unknown world, no one has to face the road entirely alone.
